sections.h2: Where is the Meigs County Recorder and when is it open?
sections.html:
The Meigs County Recorder is at 100 E. Second Street in Pomeroy, Ohio 45769. The Ohio Legal Help directory lists weekday hours from eight in the morning until four in the afternoon. The office makes a complete and permanent record of every document that transfers, mortgages or otherwise charges land in the county.

For a seller, that record is the paper trail a title company reads before closing. If a lien, an old mortgage or a gap in the chain of owners shows up there, it has to be cleared before a buyer can take clean title.

sections.h2: What are the Meigs County recording charges?
sections.html:
Recording fees are set by the state in sections 317.32 and 317.36 of the Ohio Revised Code, and the Ohio Recorders' Association summarizes them. Half of each fee is the basic recording fee and half goes to the Ohio Housing Trust Fund. A county may also add a preservation surcharge of no more than $5 per document. Ask the Meigs County Recorder whether that surcharge applies before you send payment.

Standard Ohio recording fees as published by the Ohio Recorders' Association
Document or serviceFee
Deed, mortgage, lease, easement or land contract, first two pages$34.00
Each additional page$8.00
Release, assignment or affidavit that references a prior documentBase fee plus $4.00 per reference
Document that fails the state format rules$20.00
Federal tax lien$5.00
Military dischargeNo fee

Copy fees vary by county, so ask the Meigs office for its charge on plain and certified copies.

sections.h2: How much is the Meigs County conveyance fee?
sections.html:
The county auditor's page says the Meigs County conveyance fee is $4.00 per thousand dollars of the sale price. The same rate applies to real estate and to manufactured homes. This is the charge people call the transfer tax, and it is collected at the auditor's office rather than the recorder's.

The auditor's forms page carries DTE Form 100, the statement of value and receipt, and DTE Form 100EX for exempt transfers. It also carries DTE Form 101, the statement of conveyance of homestead property. The auditor's site also lists conveyance standards dated July 1, 2025. Read them before a surveyor or attorney drafts a legal description.

A used manufactured home sold after January 1, 2000 must be transferred through the auditor, with a 50-cent transfer fee added to the conveyance fee. The clerk of courts can then transfer the title without charging sales tax.

sections.h2: How does Meigs County value a house and hear an appeal?
sections.html:
The auditor says all real property in Ohio is valued at its estimated fair market value, the price it would bring in an arm's-length sale. The auditor's office reviews building permits, land splits and boundary surveys, and inspects new construction.

A valuation complaint goes to the Board of Revision. The auditor is its permanent secretary, and the county treasurer and the president of the county commissioners sit with the auditor. Complaints must reach the auditor's office on or before March 31 of each year, on forms from that office or on DTE Form 1.

An owner-occupied home can also earn the 2.5 percent reduction. The auditor lists three conditions and a window:

  • You own the home.
  • It is your principal place of residence.
  • You apply between January 1 and the first Monday in June.

The reduction does not cover rentals, homes owned by corporations or partnerships, or acreage beyond the first acre.

sections.h2: What shapes land and houses in Meigs County?
sections.html:
Meigs County was formally established April 1, 1819 from parts of Gallia and Athens counties and was named for Ohio's fourth governor. Wikipedia gives its area as 433 square miles. The Ohio River forms the eastern and southern edges, across from West Virginia, and Vinton, Athens and Gallia counties bound it in Ohio. The seat of government is Pomeroy, and Middleport is the largest village. Racine, Rutland and Syracuse are the other villages.

The county sits on the Appalachian Plateau, so the land is rolling to rugged. Shade River and Leading Creek drain most of it. Strip and underground coal mining shaped parts of the county from the late nineteenth century, and the Yellowbush mine near Racine opened in 2009 and closed in 2015. The auditor's forms page links a document titled Developing on Abandoned Mine Land, which is worth reading if a parcel you plan to sell sits on old workings.

sections.h2: How many people and homes does Meigs County have?
sections.html:
QuickFacts, the Census Bureau's county table, puts Meigs County at 21,587 people in July 2025, a drop of 2.8 percent since the 2020 count. Housing rows from the 2020 to 2024 survey period read as follows.

  • About three of every four households (75.4 percent) own their home, out of 9,102 households.
  • The middle owner-occupied house is valued at $119,300.
  • Owners with a mortgage report $1,130 a month in costs, and those without one report $473.
  • Renters pay $722 at the median.
  • Household income is $46,873 at the median.
  • No building permits were recorded for the county in 2025.

The 2020 census found 10,649 housing units and a 13.6 percent vacancy rate, so roughly one home in seven stood empty when the census was taken.

sections.h2: What should Meigs County owners of manufactured homes know?
sections.html:
The Meigs County Auditor keeps a separate page on manufactured homes. Homes bought after January 1, 2000 are taxed like real property under the appraisal method, with values reset every three years at 35 percent of estimated market value. Older homes may stay on the depreciation method or make a one-time switch to the appraisal method after all taxes are paid.

  • Owners must register a home with the auditor within 30 days of locating it in the county, and a failure to register can bring a $100 fine.
  • A relocation notice, required to move a home on a public road, costs $5 at the auditor's office and requires that taxes be paid.
  • A home on a permanent foundation on land the owner also owns may qualify to be taxed as real estate after the title is inactivated and surrendered.

If you plan to sell a manufactured home that has moved or changed tax methods, call the auditor first so the transfer paperwork matches the home's status.

sections.h2: Where do Meigs County parcel maps and boundary questions go?
sections.html: The auditor's site says the county tax map office now runs its own website at meigscountytaxmap.com. Land splits and boundary surveys go through the tax map department before the auditor reviews them for new values, so a seller who is dividing a parcel should start there. Ask that office for the current requirements before you order a survey.

sections.h2: What documents show up when a Meigs County house changes hands?
sections.html:
Most sales involve a deed and, if the seller owed money, a mortgage release. Each one is recorded on its own and priced by page. A release or assignment also carries the per-reference charge shown in the table above.

  • Warranty or fiduciary deed from seller to buyer.
  • Mortgage release recorded after payoff.
  • Affidavit or court certificate when an estate is the seller.

If the lender has started a foreclosure, the auditor's page points owners to the county sheriff's website at meigssheriff.org for the list of upcoming sheriff's sales.

faqs.q: What is the address and phone number for the Meigs County Recorder?
faqs.a: The office is at 100 E. Second Street, Pomeroy, Ohio 45769. Ohio Legal Help lists weekday hours of eight to four.

faqs.q: How much does Meigs County charge for filing a deed?
faqs.a: The Ohio Recorders' Association lists $34.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 for each added page. A county may add a preservation surcharge of up to $5. Call the recorder to get the exact total for your page count.

faqs.q: How much is the conveyance fee on a Meigs County sale?
faqs.a: The county auditor lists $4.00 per thousand dollars of the sale price for both real estate and manufactured homes. A 50-cent transfer fee also applies to manufactured homes. Ask the auditor which form your deed needs.

faqs.q: When must a Meigs County valuation complaint be filed?
faqs.a: By March 31 of the year you are contesting. File it with the county auditor, who is secretary of the Board of Revision. Forms are available from the auditor's office.

faqs.q: Does recording a military discharge cost anything in Meigs County?
faqs.a: No. Ohio sets no fee for recording a military discharge, and the Ohio Recorders' Association fee list shows it as free.
